item.title: Jealous media attack Sydney Sweeney’s sports ad while her $2B valuation proves she’s the ultimate boss
item.description: Sydney Sweeney's Novig stake surged from $500 million to $2 billion after her viral sports ad sparked fierce debate over women's sports imagery.
item.content:encoded:
The face (and body) of a betting site just won big on her own gamble.

Actress Sydney Sweeney, who bought a stake in the peer-to-peer sports trading company Novig, has watched its valuation jump from $500 million to $2 billion in a matter of months.

How much she actually invested in the company is unknown. How much she influenced the company's growth seems undeniable. Her scantily-clad advertisement — in which she donned an array of sports attire that covered just enough to clear broadcast standards — sent Novig's name ricocheting across social media in the middle of last month.

SYDNEY SWEENEY LEAVES LITTLE TO THE IMAGINATION IN PROVOCATIVE NEW CAMPAIGN

Writers and athletes buried Sweeney with criticism — particularly in regard to her representation of women in sports. But the "Euphoria" star brushed all the hate off her shoulder pads and proved once again ... that all Sweeney does is win.

This is yet another example of how activists and a significant portion of the media failed to represent the general population. Ava Stampa of the Rocky Mountain Collegian wrote a piece with the headline: "Sydney Sweeney is a disgrace to feminism, women's sports." Guardian sports columnist Jane McManus penned a similar piece with the headline reading "Sydney Sweeney's prediction ad is cynical, unhealthy and reveals plenty about modern sports." USA Today's Nancy Armour, meanwhile, wrote that Novig running the ad was an attempt to "demean the sweat and sacrifice of women athletes?"

RIDICULOUS USA TODAY COLUMN PROVES THAT THE DEMAND FOR MISOGYNY IN SPORTS FAR EXCEEDS THE SUPPLY

Oh, come on.

Never mind that, for years, ESPN Magazine ran its annual "Body Issue," which showed male and female athletes of all shapes and sizes posing nude with strategic modesty. And the idea that someone might see Sweeney's ad and change their thoughts on women's sports is about as absurd as a bigot seeing an "End Racism" slogan and having an epiphany.

It was an ad that used sex appeal to catch the eye of a mostly-male market — not a "kick in the face" to female athletes, as four-time Olympic swimming gold medalist Ariarne Titmus suggested.

Plus, isn't Sweeney doing exactly what so much of the Left endorses these days? She's a girl boss who bought equity in a company and took action to get herself paid. She's embracing her sexuality and using it to further empower herself. The disdain liberal media outlets hurl at her isn't because Sweeney defied their values. It's because she's a freakin' smoke show.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS WHAT OTHER GASLIGHTING FEMALE ATHLETES WON'T ABOUT THE NAKED SYDNEY SWEENEY AD

Exactly how much Sweeney's ad contributed to Novig's fourfold increase in valuation since February is impossible to know. But saying the spot added at least a few hundred million dollars to that valuation is hardly a wild guess. And this isn't the first time Sydney sent a company's stock price soaring. When American Eagle unveiled its equally controversial "Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans" campaign in July 2025, its shares jumped 10 percent in a single day.

The contempt critics have for her isn't rooted in principle. It's rooted in jealousy. But that contempt doesn't reflect the every man (or every woman).

Sweeney does, in fact, have great genes. They're on display from head to toe and between the ears. She may not be the athlete she poses as in her commercial — but she does know how to get a victory.

item.title: A'ja Wilson's mom freaks out when asked to explain her 'Love Beats Hate' sign after Game 3 win vs Fever
item.description: A'ja Wilson's mom Eva paraded a "Love Beats Hate" sign after the Aces' series-clinching win, but her courtside confrontation with an Outkick reporter told a different story.
item.content:encoded:
The discourse surrounding A'ja Wilson's unsportsmanlike actions in Game 2 in Indiana, where she received no repercussions from the league, even though she entered the seating area and confronted a male Fever fan for simply pointing at her after a controversial foul, has sparked countless inflammatory comments.

Las Vegas Aces' fans have condemned the man and, at times, the entire fan base. The media has overwhelming taken Wilson's side, even after the man was proven innocent, and players like Chicago Sky's Natasha Cloud claimed the fan may be a domestic abuser. Even A'ja Wilson's mom jumped on the bandwagon in her own special way following the Aces' series-clinching win in Vegas Thursday night.

After the game, where Wilson dominated yet again, leading all scorers with 36 points, along with 10 rebounds, Wilson was seen hugging team owner Mark Davis, as well as friends, and her mother, Eva Rakes Wilson. Following congratulating her daughter, Eva began waving a pink, heart-shaped sign that said "Love Beats Hate." It seemed to imply the baseless claim & unfounded talking point we've heard for years now – especially after Wilson's confrontation with the fan in Indiana – that Fever fans are hateful bigots. Some fans I interviewed outside the arena told me outright, and unashamedly, that they believe Fever fans are "racist." But without asking Eva personally about her sign, I wouldn't know for sure what she was implying. Luckily, I was provided that opportunity minutes later.

WNBA VETERAN NATASHA CLOUD SMEARS FEVER FAN WITH WILD DOMESTIC ABUSE CLAIM OVER POINTING FINGER AT A'JA WILSON

Eva began walking the circumference of the court, parading the sign across the arena with Aces fans cheering her on. I told myself I would ask her to explain her sign if she made it back my way.

As she was walking in the pathway behind the courtside seats, still proudly displaying the sign, looking for more validation from fans, I asked her calmly and respectfully, "Can you tell me what your sign means?"

Eva responded sternly to my question with a question: "What do you think it means?" A nearby supporter yelled at me saying, "Read it!"

PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT

I told her and the fan, "I'm reading it, but I'm interested what it means."

She continued to deflect, asking me: "What do you think it means?"

I asked again, which she responded saying, "It means exactly what the sign says."

At this point, you could see how incredibly frustrated she was as I calmly attempted to get her to explain what statement she is making exactly. "Listen to me!" she exclaimed as she stepped back towards me.

At this point I needed to get to the bottom of this and ask the question we were all thinking. "Do you believe Indiana Fever fans are hateful?" That really struck a cord as she started stepping towards me again and pointing in my face. (Oh the irony of A'ja Wilson's mom pointing and stepping toward me. I thought that was one of the worst things a person could do courtside.)

"I mean exactly what the sign says," she yelled again, pacing back and forth, clearly ticked off that I would even dare question her.

She then pointed in my face again and said, "Keep it (the camera) rolling!" followed by putting the sign in my face. I then responded with, "That seems like a lot of hate," referencing the way she was acting toward my questioning and my understanding of the accusations she was leveling at Fever fans.

A female fan nearby then laughably claimed that I was "provoking her," which I refuted stating, "I'm simply asking. I'm legitimately asking do you believe Indiana Fever fans [are hateful]." Eva than snapped again, aggressively pointing in my face yelling, "What do you think it means?!"

WNBA REVEALS WHY A'JA WILSON WAS NOT EJECTED FOR APPROACHING FEVER FAN DURING PLAYOFF GAME

The female Aces fan then claimed I was "instigating" in my interaction with Eva, which I refuted, saying, "I'm the calm one here simply asking her what that sign means."

That's where Eva walked away.

If this proves anything, it's that the apple doesn't fall far from the tree. If you wanted to understand why A'ja Wilson would get so rageful because a Fever fan simply pointed at her and said, "It (the foul) is on you," it may be because she has a mother that loses her mind about someone daring to question the narrative that the Aces vs. Fever match-up was essentially good vs. evil.

If you're willing to parade around an arena making a statement with a sign, you should at least be able to defend your stance, not resort to fits of rage, while refusing to answer simple questions.

For someone that claims to be on the side of love, I really wasn't feeling it here.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Let this be a lesson that we cannot allow irrational people like Eva Wilson, and her defenders, to insinuate that Fever or Caitlin Clark fans are the hateful, divisive ones. Don't allow them to gaslight you into believing you're the problem. This kind of rhetoric is why many sports fans don't care to support A'ja Wilson, and many other WNBA players, who have either implied, or overtly stated, that Fever fans are hateful.

To be honest, I have never seen a fanbase more vilified and slandered than Fever and Caitlin Clark fans. Matt Calkins’ piece, which he authored on Thursday, titled "Players and media hate Fever fans for one simple reason: They think they're conservative," is spot on. This is all political to them. Though they have been begging for eyeballs on their league for years, they can't stand those viewers they've been praying for, who may be on the opposite side of the political aisle than them. They see any pushback or lack of conformity to their left-wing activism as a threat that must be labeled as "hateful."

Again, I can only speculate about the specific meaning of Eva's sign, because she refused to answer my questions, but I don't think it could be any more clear than what I laid out in this piece. It would suggest that she might believe Fever fans are hateful and the Aces fanbase, as well as her daughter, represent love.

I didn't feel the love in this interaction, and neither did that fan, who was verbally berated by A'ja Wilson for doing nothing more than pointing at her from over 20 feet away.

item.title: Inside the House GOP's 4-week battle plan to save its majority
item.description: House GOP Chairwoman Lisa McClain reveals the four key topics Republicans plan to hammer home in the final weeks before the November midterms.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: House GOP leaders are quietly laying their battle plans for the final month ahead of the November midterm elections.

A new memo being sent to Republicans across the country, first obtained by Fox News Digital, reveals four key topics that the House GOP is focusing on in the final four weeks before the election: the border, fraudulent use of taxpayer dollars, the economy, and public safety.

"I think these are the points that the voters actually care most about," House GOP Chairwoman Lisa McClain, R-Mich., who leads Republicans' messaging strategy, told Fox News Digital. "[Democrats] want open borders. They want to defund the police, they want to take more money out of your pocket and give it to somebody else. They believe in bigger government. We believe in people... So those are the things that we're really hammering home during this election."

It comes as Republicans fight an uphill battle to keep control of Congress for the latter half of President Donald Trump's final term.

REPUBLICANS FACE BRUTAL MIDTERM HEADWINDS. SIX FORCES COULD HELP THEM DEFY HISTORY.

A recent Fox News poll found Democrats have a wider path to victory than Republicans in the House. Democrats are projected to win 215 seats compared to 201 for the GOP, meaning the left only needs three more victories out of the 19 possible toss-up races to clinch a majority. Republicans would need to win at least 17 of those races.

10 DEMOCRAT-HELD HOUSE SEATS REPUBLICANS COULD FLIP TO SAVE THEIR MAJORITY

Republicans are also seeing political opportunity in the far-left insurgency that's gripped the Democratic Party during its primary cycle, warning that socialists are pushing the party further left than the majority of Americans.

On the economy, which is a focus of week two in the GOP memo, Republican incumbents and candidates are encouraged to talk about "putting more money back in Americans' pockets and creating more opportunities to get ahead through hard work, ownership, and economic freedom."

HOUSE CONSERVATIVES UNLEASH MULTIMILLION-DOLLAR MIDTERM BLITZ AGAINST DEM 'SOCIALIST' INSURGENCY

The economy, including high grocery and gas prices, has become a central issue in the 2026 election cycle.

Democrats have seized on Americans' struggle with cost-of-living as a political cudgel against Republicans, particularly using Trump's tariffs on allies like Canada and his war in Iran as arguments against the GOP.

McClain acknowledged Americans' concerns, urging Republicans to be forthright with their voters but warning that Democrats' high-tax policies would worsen the situation. She also pointed to the low poverty rate and Trump's new trade deals as positives the GOP could highlight.

"What we're not going to do is gaslight the American people, right? That's what the Democrats did, and it didn't work well for them," she said, referencing former President Joe Biden's handling of high inflation during his term. "But you have to take a look at the alternative. The alternative is absolutely terrifying."

"We had a massive hole that we were digging out of under Biden. We have more work to do, of course we do, but do you want our trajectory, or do you want to go back to 9% inflation, open borders, and, and higher taxes? Because I tell everybody, every single Democrat voted to raise your taxes. They want more of your money."

She echoed Trump's assurances that gas prices would drop when the conflict with Iran ended, adding, "We also don't want the number one state sponsor of terror to have a nuclear weapon, and we have to protect Americans from that."

Meanwhile, Trump's polling is underwater, with the most recent Fox News survey from mid-September finding his disapproval rating at 61%. Trump's favorability remains a high 79% with Republican voters, however, meaning the GOP could still prevail by turning out the base on Nov. 3.

One of the most decisive issues of his 2024 victory proved to be illegal immigration and the border, a fervor Republicans are hoping they can harness again come November.

The memo encouraged Republicans to discuss "protecting America by stopping illegal immigration, enforcing our laws, and knowing who is entering the country."

McClain pointed to policies promoted by far-left Democrats like abolishing police — and some mainstream Democrats' backing of sanctuary jurisdictions — as a contrast point for the election, while arguing Republicans were still supportive of legal immigration.

"They tell you they want to defund the police. They tell you they want sanctuary cities. These are their words, not mine. These are the policies...they want," McClain said. "The Republicans, we want immigration, we believe in immigration, but we want people to come in the right way and we darn sure want to make sure we know who's coming across."

item.title: Trump’s first-year government overhaul delivers change Washington hasn’t seen since the 1960s
item.description: IRS audit revenue dropped 35% after nearly 10,000 agents were let go, raising questions about whether federal workforce cuts are saving money.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration has reduced the federal workforce to the lowest point in roughly 60 years, according to newly released data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

As of August, just 2.67 million people were employed by the federal government, down from just over 3 million when President Donald Trump took office, marking the lowest headcount since 1966, per the BLS.

The administration has estimated those cuts will produce significant savings, with OPM projecting that its Deferred Resignation Program alone will save more than $20 billion a year. But the reductions have also come with costs.

Revenue collected from IRS examinations fell 35%, from about $10 billion in fiscal 2024 to $6.5 billion in fiscal 2025, as the agency was undergoing steep workforce reductions that ultimately cut examination and collection staffing by nearly 10,000 employees, according to a Treasury watchdog.

APPEALS COURT UPHOLDS ORDER BLOCKING IRS FROM SHARING TAXPAYER DATA WITH ICE

Former President Joe Biden secured nearly $80 billion in 2022 for the IRS over 10 years to upgrade its systems, improve taxpayer service and hire more staff, including enforcement personnel.

The Trump administration has proposed further IRS cuts for 2027.

Not all agencies have been hit the same by the Trump administration’s cuts.

The Departments of Education, Agriculture and Housing and Urban Development have been cut particularly hard, whereas headcount at the Department of Homeland Security, which has been responsible for carrying out much of the president’s immigration agenda, has remained largely unchanged.

TRUMP’S $5K CHECKS COULD JOIN STACK OF PAST UNFULFILLED PROMISES, FORMER CONGRESS BUDGET CHIEF WARNS

Not included in the BLS’ count of government employees are the roughly 1.35 million members of the armed services or the approximately 100,000 people employed by intelligence agencies.

Cutting the size of the federal workforce, a project that was eventually spearheaded by the Department of Government Efficiency and the Office of Personnel Management, was a major campaign promise during Trump’s 2024 run as he vowed to slim down what he said was a bloated government. 

OFFICE OF PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT UNCOVERS $500M IN FRAUD AND WASTE IN FEDERAL HEALTH BENEFITS PROGRAMS

GAO found that agencies spent about $6.7 billion paying employees who took part in the Deferred Resignation Program, which allowed many of them to stop working while still collecting a paycheck until they officially left government. The Partnership for Public Service also estimated the government spent $12.1 million rehiring workers who had previously been fired during the administration’s workforce reductions.

Despite the cuts, most of which happened during the president’s first year in office, the Trump administration spent 3% more on federal salaries during its first year in power than the Biden administration did during its initial year.

If Republicans win the midterm elections, the president has promised to cut $5,000 checks to all adult American citizens, a long-shot promise that, if followed through on, would cost the nation between $1.2 trillion and $1.35 trillion.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital.

item.title: Kash Patel defends FBI's ‘Most Wanted’ busts amid manipulation accusations, highlights 'Summer Heat' success
item.description: Kash Patel defends the FBI's Most Wanted list amid scrutiny, pointing to Operation Summer Heat 2.0's 8,900-plus arrests and record seizures.
item.content:encoded:
FBI Director Kash Patel pushed back against critics questioning the agency's Most Wanted fugitive statistics, framing the scrutiny as an attack on rank-and-file agents while pointing to surging arrest and seizure figures in the recently completed "Operation Summer Heat 2.0" as proof of a revamped, field-centric agency.

Patel dismissed news reports that the FBI allegedly fudged its Most Wanted captures as attempts to "denigrate the work of the bureau," insisting that career staff manage the lists independently of political leadership.

In September, Patel revealed that the FBI apprehended all 10 members of the FBI's Most Wanted list during President Donald Trump's second term. On Wednesday, an MS NOW report from May resurfaced in which FBI officials said the agency has been placing fugitives on the Most Wanted list whose capture was impending.

"Look, it's really simple," Patel told Fox News Digital. "The FBI's Most Wanted list and any other campaign we're putting on has been going on for at least 75 years. The career staff at the bureau manage that list. They look and say, 'Who's the target of opportunity? Who can we get? Who's the worst perpetrator who's been on the run?' and then they announce it. I literally don't have anything to do with it."

KASH PATEL REVEALS FBI'S CAPTURE OF ALL 10 MEMBERS OF MOST WANTED FUGITIVES LIST DURING HEARING

"I just think that those critics out there are super unpleased with the fact that the Trump administration and this FBI delivered on what used to be an apolitical mission of keeping law enforcement at the top and protecting our American citizens," he added.

PATEL SAYS FBI HAS CUT BUREAUCRACY, MOVED 1,000 AGENTS TO FIELD OFFICES IN 'GENERATIONAL' OVERHAUL

Patel attributed the agency's wave of high-profile arrests, record-high fentanyl seizures and weapons seized under the recently completed Operation Summer Heat 2.0 to a sweeping restructuring of the organization that permanently relocated nearly 2,000 FBI personnel to various field offices across the country and gutted Washington's bureaucracy.

The FBI, he said, has transitioned from short-term crime "surges" into a permanent, field-centric enforcement posture designed to drive down violent crime year-round.

KASH PATEL TOUTS FBI 'FULL-THROTTLE MISSION' AFTER OPERATION SPRING CLEANING YIELDS 615 INDICTMENTS/COMPLAINTS

Operation Summer Heat 2.0 was the second iteration of an operation of the same name launched in 2025 — a nationwide federal law enforcement surge targeting violent crime, street gangs and drug trafficking networks. From June through August, FBI agents, in conjunction with local authorities, went after suspected criminals in various metropolitan areas.

"You have to talk to the American people. You have to show up in the field, and you have to drive resources and permanently place people and technology in the field," Patel said. "That was the sort of overarching approach to striking at the heart of violent crime."

As a result, authorities made more than 8,900 arrests, up 3% from last summer's Summer Heat initiative.

In addition, 5,013 weapons were seized — a 120% jump compared to last year's operation — more than 1,400 children were identified or located, a 34% jump, and authorities conducted 687 fentanyl seizures, up 63%, the FBI said.

KASH PATEL TO TOUT 'LARGEST' YEAR-TO-YEAR VIOLENT CRIME DROP IN US HISTORY

"So from last year to this year, we wanted to run that playbook for Summer Heat 2.0, and the only thing we did a little differently was we added even more bodies to the field," Patel said. "So the enterprise-wide lift, shift, focus, and pivot was: we're not on defense anymore. In order to catch violent criminals and defend the homeland, you have to go on offense."

This year's operation expanded on last year's through inter-agency collaboration and other measures, Patel said, which yielded significant safety returns across urban areas.

"Just to show you that it's working in every single city and major metropolis across the country, last year for the first time, America saw 1.1 million fewer violent aggravated assaults, rapes, robberies, and homicides," Patel said. "That's 1.1 million fewer victims across the country because of what the federal government, the Bureau, and our partners were able to bring to bear across the country."

item.title: Iraq sounds alarm on terror threat from Syria one day after US troops leave
item.description: Iraq's foreign minister warns ISIS fighters could cross from Syria as Baghdad prepares its forces just one day after the U.S. military withdrawal.
item.content:encoded:
Iraq is preparing for the possibility that Islamic State fighters could spill across the border from Syria, the country's foreign minister said Thursday. It comes just one day after the U.S. military formally ended its counter-ISIS mission in Iraq.

Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein told reporters in Washington, D.C., on Thursday that Baghdad is closely watching recent ISIS activity in neighboring Syria, and warned that fighters crossing into Iraq could once again pose a threat to the country's security.

"We are worried about ISIS activities inside Syria," Hussein said, adding that Iraqi forces were preparing to confront any movement toward the border. Still, he stressed that Baghdad believes its military can now handle the terrorist group without the large U.S.-led coalition presence that helped defeat ISIS's self-declared caliphate.

ISIS POISED TO EXPLOIT HISTORIC US IRAQ EXIT, TERROR GROUP 'ACTIVELY WAITING IN THE GAPS,' EXPERT WARNS

"If they would be capable to cross the border, that would be once again a threat to our security," Hussein said. "We are preparing ourselves – if there will be any movement from inside Iraq — to fight them and to defeat them."

The warning came just after the departure of the final U.S. forces under Operation Inherent Resolve on Wednesday.

US FACES ANOTHER MAJOR MIDDLE EAST TROOP WITHDRAWAL, BUT THREAT REMAINS

Trump hailed the withdrawal as a victory over ISIS, saying the terrorist group had been "completely decimated."

"We came to fight a caliphate, and there is no longer a caliphate, so we are going home," Trump said. "This day is a victory for the United States, a victory for Iraq, and a decisive victory over ISIS."

But Hussein's warning came four days after Syrian authorities said they dismantled an ISIS cell operating across four provinces, arresting four of its leaders and seizing explosives that had been prepared for attacks. The cell had carried out kidnappings and was involved in assassinations and planting explosive devices, according to Syrian security forces.

U.S. officials assess that ISIS has been severely degraded and no longer poses a systemic threat to Iraq, but the terrorist group maintains scattered cells across Iraq and Syria. The Pentagon has said Iraqi forces are capable of suppressing the remaining threat themselves, while U.S. forces continue counter-ISIS operations in Syria aimed at preventing the group from reconstituting.

The withdrawal marked the end of a U.S. military mission in Iraq that, in different forms, stretched across more than two decades and reshaped American foreign policy. The 2003 invasion toppled Saddam Hussein but gave way to years of insurgency and sectarian violence. Nearly 4,500 U.S. service members were killed before American forces withdrew in 2011.

Three years later, U.S. troops returned as ISIS swept across large parts of Iraq and Syria, seizing Mosul and declaring a self-styled caliphate. The U.S. launched Operation Inherent Resolve in 2014, leading an international coalition that helped Iraqi forces reclaim the territory ISIS had captured.

After the withdrawal, Iraq intends to pursue a bilateral security relationship with the U.S., though discussions on what that will look like have not yet begun.

He said Baghdad and Washington had discussed the principle of a future security relationship while negotiating the coalition’s departure, but still need to work out the details, including what kind of training, intelligence sharing or other military cooperation could continue.

At the same time, Baghdad is moving to bring Iran-backed militia groups operating outside the regular security forces under government control, another longstanding source of friction between Iraq and the U.S.

Iraq had originally set a Sept. 30 deadline — coinciding with the U.S.-led coalition’s withdrawal — for armed groups to lay down their weapons or come under state authority. That deadline has since slipped to June 2027 as some powerful factions resist disarmament.

Hussein said one group had issued a statement Thursday backing the government’s plan and another was expected to follow within a day, while negotiations continued with others.

"A single group will not be allowed to take the decision in their hands and attack other countries," Hussein said.

That question has taken on new urgency as Iraq tries to contain the fallout from the war between the U.S. and neighboring Iran. Hussein confirmed that a recent attack on Saudi Arabia originated from Iraqi territory near the Iranian border, prompting an investigation by Baghdad and consultations with both Riyadh and Tehran.

Hussein said he had been in contact with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan over the attack and planned to visit Riyadh to discuss the matter further. The investigation remains ongoing, he said.

More broadly, Hussein described Iraq as caught in the middle of the U.S.-Iran conflict, saying Iraqi territory had been struck by both sides.

"We became a victim of this war," Hussein said.

Baghdad has pressed both Washington and Tehran to resolve the conflict through negotiations, Hussein said, while seeking to keep Iraq from being drawn further into the fighting.

item.title: This amount of deli meat associated with higher dementia risk in compelling new review
item.description: A major review links just two daily slices of deli meat to a 44% higher dementia risk, raising questions about ultra-processed foods and brain health. Experts weigh in.
item.content:encoded:
Eating just two slices of deli meat a day was associated with a substantially higher risk of dementia, according to a new review of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) and brain health.

The findings, published in the August 2026 issue of Annual Review of Nutrition, looked at dozens of human and animal studies, including one involving nearly 500,000 people in the U.K. The study found that each additional 25 grams of processed meat eaten daily corresponded with a 44% higher risk of all-cause dementia and a 52% higher risk of Alzheimer's.

Twenty-five grams of processed meat equals roughly one to two slices of deli meat, depending on how thick the meat is sliced.

JUST ONE SMALL SERVING OF ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD A DAY LINKED TO HIGHER DISEASE RISK, MAJOR STUDY FINDS

The review, done by an international team of 27 researchers, looked more broadly at whether diets high in UPFs may contribute to brain aging over time. 

UPFs include sugary drinks, packaged snacks and other heavily industrially processed foods that often contain ingredients such as emulsifiers, preservatives and artificial colors.

"The main takeaway for consumers is that it is very easy to get food items into the food supply without really understanding what kinds of effects they have on health, including the health of the brain," lead author Owen Carmichael, Ph.D., of the Pennington Biomedical Research Center in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, told Fox News Digital.

Some UPFs are so highly engineered that they "look like pharmaceuticals," Carmichael said. 

5 ULTRA-PROCESSED FOODS THAT MAY BE WORSE FOR YOUR HEALTH THAN YOU THINK, EXPERT SAYS

"Yet they don't face anywhere near the scrutiny pharmaceuticals face when trying to get on the market," he added. "When it comes to food safety, we sort of shoot first and ask questions later."

Carmichael said researchers are investigating two leading theories on why UPFs are linked to brain health. 

One is that UPFs can damage heart and blood vessel health, indirectly affecting the brain. "Healthy heart, healthy mind," he said.

In general, he said UPFs are "especially bad for your health from the neck down, damaging the heart, blood vessels, muscle, fat [and] liver."

The other theory is that certain food additives may disrupt brain chemistry.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Both theories need further research, Carmichael said. 

Much of the current research still comes from animal studies, according to the review, and long-term randomized clinical trials are still lacking.

The authors emphasized that the findings are observational and cannot prove that processed meat, which includes deli turkey, ham, salami, bacon, hot dogs and sausages, directly causes dementia.

But for people looking to improve long-term brain health, Carmichael's "healthy heart, healthy mind" rule still applies. 

Many dietary recommendations overlap with long-standing heart-health advice, such as eating more fruits, vegetables and fish.

The review cited research suggesting that replacing just 10% of calories from UPFs with unprocessed foods could lower dementia risk by 19%. Ultra-processed foods make up about 55% of Americans’ daily calories, experts note.

UPFs tend to be inexpensive, convenient and heavily marketed — making them easy for many people to consume regularly, Dr. William Scott Burgin, a vascular neurologist at the University of South Florida and chief medical officer for NeuroEM Therapeutics, told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"UPFs are probably the worst for brain health," said Burgin, who was not involved with the new research. 

But he cautioned against lumping all UPFs together. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"There are foods that get technically classified as ultra-processed, but are more likely neutral or may even be good for you, such as fortified whole grain cereals, dairy-based foods like yogurt, and packaged breads and grain products."

Burgin also noted that most of the evidence comes from observational studies rather than research assigning people to specific diets.

"All that being said, while I encourage people to reduce their consumption of UPFs, a cookie every now and then is not a problem," he said.

He also encouraged a diet rich in omega-3s, antioxidants and polyphenols, while noting that some evidence also supports supplements such as B vitamins.

Fox News Digital reached out to The Meat Institute, headquartered in Virginia, and The American Association of Meat Processors, based in Pennsylvania, for comment.

item.title: Pills found near dead Ole Miss student didn't come from gas station after feds raid store, owner says

item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The owner of the gas station where investigators say Robert Strang bought synthetic kratom denies that the pills found near the student's body came from his store.

Court documents show that Ole Miss students Strang, 20, and Aidan Hamilton, 18, were found dead on Sept. 21, each discovered near similar packages of synthetic kratom. Authorities said Hamilton "could have died due to a Pulmonary Edema," a conclusion consistent with a drug overdose. First responders who arrived at Strang's residence near campus found him "cold to the touch," according to dispatch audio.

A narcotics agent wrote in an affidavit that the pills found near both students were Smax Pseudo-DHM, and listed pseudoindoxyl and MGM-15(DHM) among the ingredients found on the pack near Hamilton. The Drug Enforcement Administration temporarily placed mitragynine pseudoindoxyl in Schedule I on Aug. 26, which bars its sale.

A Mississippi law enforcement agent investigating the Ole Miss students' deaths said he believes "pseudoindoxyl" refers to that compound, and lab results confirming the pills' contents are pending, court documents say.

KRATOM INDUSTRY WARNS SYNTHETIC OPIOIDS SHOULD NOT BE CALLED 'KRATOM'

After speaking with Strang's roommates, agents learned he had been buying "Smax" pills at Express Mart #7, a gas station in Water Valley, Mississippi, a little over 20 minutes from Ole Miss. An undercover Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics agent later bought a similar form of Smax Pseudo pills at the store. The package lists pseudoindoxyl as its ingredient, which the narcotics agent says he believes is short for mitragynine pseudoindoxyl.

Ibrahim Aydah, the owner of the gas station, told Fox News Digital he doesn't believe the "Smax" pills found near Strang came from his store. He said he doesn't put price labels on his products, while the pack near Strang had a price on it, also claiming he doesn't carry the 200 mg version.

VAPE STORE ARRESTS NEAR OLE MISS CAMPUS NOT BELIEVED TO BE LINKED TO TWO STUDENT DEATHS, STATE OFFICIAL SAYS

"The package that I see on the news, it wasn't from my store," Aydah said. "The package...the Smax is 200. I never carry 200. And it has different ingredients in it than mine."

According to court documents, a store clerk told the undercover agent that they were out of the 200 mg version.

POLICE NEAR OLE MISS RESPOND TO SUSPECTED OVERDOSE, SAY 'NOT STUDENT-RELATED'

Aydah said federal agents seized all of the kratom products in his store Friday, and said he wishes he would have gotten notice from the federal government that he was carrying illegal products.

"Yes, they took all my stuff. I lost everything and it's a law." Aydah said. "The federal law bans it. I was shocked."

A spokeswoman for the DEA told Fox News Digital that the agency executed a search warrant at the gas station on Friday, noting that it's part of an "ongoing investigation."

item.title: Trump’s Iran crackdown collides with NATO ally seeking access to America’s prized fighter jet
item.description: U.S.-sanctioned Iranian airlines made at least 83 flights into Turkey after a key Treasury deadline, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies says.
item.content:encoded:
At least 83 flights operated by U.S.-sanctioned Iranian airlines landed in Turkey in the five days after a key American sanctions deadline, according to flight data analyzed by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, putting a new spotlight on whether Washington will enforce its escalating pressure campaign against companies servicing the carriers in a NATO ally.

The Sept. 28 FDD report said U.S. pressure has helped push Iranian airlines out of several regional markets, including Iraq, the United Arab Emirates and Oman, but found that Turkey remains a significant gap in Washington’s effort to ground the carriers.

The findings come after the Treasury Department announced sweeping new sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry on Sept. 8, designating all 27 remaining active Iranian airlines under Executive Order 13902. Treasury said Iran's aviation sector has been used to transport weapons, personnel and illicit cargo and warned foreign businesses about the risks of continuing to support sanctioned carriers.

TRUMP PUSHES F-35 SALE TO TURKEY, BUT HIS OWN STATE DEPARTMENT SAYS ERDOĞAN HASN'T MET LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

The continued Iranian flights come at a sensitive moment in U.S.-Turkey relations. Turkey is a NATO ally, and President Donald Trump has publicly emphasized his close relationship with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan while signaling openness to restoring Ankara’s access to the F-35 fighter jet program. Turkey was removed from the program after purchasing Russia’s S-400 air-defense system, a move that also triggered U.S. sanctions in 2020.

During a July 2026 visit to Turkey, Trump said his administration would lift those sanctions and was considering allowing Ankara to buy F-35s, though congressional restrictions tied to Turkey’s possession of the S-400 remain an obstacle. Erdoğan said as recently as Sept. 24 that he expects Washington to take "concrete steps" toward Turkey’s return to the program.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that after a Sept. 23 wind-down deadline, companies providing sanctioned Iranian airlines with services such as fuel or landing support risked losing access to the U.S. financial system. FDD cited Bessent saying that by that date, Iranian airlines would be "shut down around the world."

But FDD researchers Ahmad Sharawi and Sinan Ciddi said their review of Flightradar24 flight histories showed that at least 83 flights operated by U.S.-sanctioned Iranian carriers landed in Turkey between Sept. 23 and Sept. 27, after that deadline had passed. The flights landed in Istanbul, Ankara and Izmir, according to the report.

The researchers identified 12 sanctioned Iranian airlines among the arrivals. Iran Airtour and Caspian Airlines each accounted for 12 landings, Iran Air for 10, and ATA Airlines and AVA Airlines for nine each, according to FDD. Eight of the 12 carriers identified in the flight data were among the airlines newly designated by Treasury on Sept. 8.

IRAN LOSES KEY ECONOMIC LIFELINE IN MIDDLE EAST THAT TRUMP'S SANCTIONS COULDN'T REACH AS DEADLOCK PERSISTS

The Treasury Department told Fox News Digital that it has continued raising the issue directly with senior Turkish officials and has warned Turkish companies and financial institutions about their potential sanctions exposure.

"Following Treasury’s productive engagements with senior Turkish authorities last month, which quickly translated into tangible results — including the cancellation of Mahan Air flights and the revocation of Bank Mellat’s license — we have continued discussions regarding Türkiye’s aviation links to Iran and the sanctions exposure Turkish financial institutions and businesses face for facilitating these flights," a Treasury spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "We have made those risks clear and continue to address these issues at senior levels with the Turkish government," the spokesperson said.

The Treasury spokesperson pointed to the administration’s broader "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign, saying it was producing results as Washington seeks to cut off Iran’s remaining sources of revenue and access to international markets. "Operation Economic Outcast is delivering results as Treasury and our partners continue to sever the Iranian regime’s remaining economic lifelines," the spokesperson said. "Iran’s rial has fallen to record lows, Iran loaded no crude oil onto tankers in September, and countries across the region are taking concrete steps to restrict Iran’s access to the international financial system and commercial aviation."

"We will continue applying pressure and holding accountable those who provide the regime with the financial and commercial lifelines it needs to sustain its terrorist activities," the spokesperson added.

Turkey has indeed taken some steps to limit aviation ties with Iran. Turkish Airlines, AJet and Pegasus removed flights to Iran from their schedules, while Mahan Air suspended service to Turkey beginning Sept. 21, according to Turkish Minute, citing airline schedules and reporting by the Financial Times and other outlets.

Mahan Air has been under U.S. sanctions since 2011. The Treasury Department said at the time that the airline provided financial, material and technological support to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force.

Other sanctioned Iranian airlines, however, have continued flying into Turkey. Caspian Airlines and Meraj Air were designated by Treasury as Specially Designated Global Terrorists in August 2014. Treasury said Caspian had transported IRGC personnel and weapons to Syria and said Meraj had ferried illicit cargo, including weapons, to the Syrian government.

Sharawi told Fox News Digital that the continued flights reflect a gap between Ankara’s public steps and its handling of sanctioned Iranian carriers.

"The fact that sanctioned Iranian airlines continue to land in Turkey, despite Washington’s clear effort to restrict their operations, is a testament to Ankara’s willingness to take symbolic measures while turning a blind eye to much of Iran’s broader activity," Sharawi said.

MILLIONS OF BARRELS OF IRANIAN OIL SIT BEYOND TRUMP BLOCKADE AS HE VOWS ‘ZERO LEAKAGE’

Sharawi argued that Washington could increase pressure by targeting Turkish companies that continue providing services to sanctioned Iranian carriers.

"Ankara may think it can get away with this, but Washington has not hesitated in the past to sanction Turkish entities that support sanctioned Iranian actors," he told Fox News Digital. "Continuing to target companies that provide that support would send a clear message to Ankara that facilitating Iran’s sanctioned networks will carry consequences."

He said such measures could have a practical effect on Iran’s ability to maintain the routes.

"If the United States targets the support system that keeps these sanctioned Iranian carriers operating, private Turkish companies will have much less incentive to continue doing business with them," Sharawi said. "If those companies begin cutting ties, it could significantly restrict Iranian airlines’ ability to operate routes to Turkey."

The Turkey findings come as another advocacy group is raising concerns about a different potential weak point in Washington’s campaign to isolate Tehran: Iranian maritime commerce in waters near Malaysia.

United Against Nuclear Iran said Sept. 25 that its investigators traveled roughly 100 nautical miles into the South China Sea near Malaysia’s Eastern Outer Port Limits, where the group said it observed Iranian-linked tankers, cargo vessels and bulk carriers alongside Malaysian bunker vessels supplying ships with fuel. UANI described the concentration of ships as a "floating city" supporting Iran’s sanctions-evasion network. Those findings were produced by UANI and have not been independently verified for this draft.

EXCLUSIVE: RUSSIAN DOCUMENT REVEALS SWEEPING IRAN PLAN SPANNING NUCLEAR, FINANCE AND AVIATION

"After seeing this floating city of ghost tankers with our own eyes, it is clear it is serving as an illicit Malaysia-backed lifeline for the Iranian regime," UANI CEO Ambassador Mark D. Wallace said in a Sept. 25 statement. He accused Malaysian entities of providing support that allows Tehran to continue generating revenue despite international efforts to economically isolate the regime.

Former Florida Gov. and UANI Chairman Jeb Bush and Wallace called on the Treasury Department to sanction entities associated with Malaysia’s Pengerang petroleum complex as well as Malaysian entities or officials they allege are facilitating the trade. Their call for sanctions is an advocacy position and does not establish that the Malaysian entities have violated U.S. law.

Fox News Digital has learned that Treasury has mapped Iranian oil-smuggling networks, facilitators and financial channels, including deceptive shipping activity off the coast of Malaysia, and that senior Treasury officials continue to raise the issue with Malaysian and other foreign government counterparts.

Taken together, the findings from FDD and UANI highlight what the organizations describe as continuing enforcement challenges as Washington attempts to cut Iran off from international aviation, shipping and financial networks. Treasury has continued expanding that campaign: on Sept. 29, it announced another round of sanctions targeting individuals and companies it said had procured weapons and components for Iran’s Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Turkish and Malaysian embassies for comment but did not receive a response.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: 128 GOP lawmakers call for federal probe into Planned Parenthood's taxpayer funding
item.description: A coalition of 128 Republican lawmakers is urging the HHS Inspector General to review Planned Parenthood's federal funding for potential fraud or abuse.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A coalition of 128 Republican lawmakers is pressing the federal government to scrutinize Planned Parenthood's taxpayer funding and potentially launch an investigation into the organization and its affiliates.

Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J., and Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., led the bicameral effort, asking Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Inspector General T. March Bell to review Planned Parenthood's federal funding and determine whether the organization and its affiliates have complied with federal laws and funding requirements.

"We write to request that the Office of Inspector General (OIG) review and, if appropriate, initiate an investigation into the activities of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and the organization's affiliates," the lawmakers wrote.

READ: DR. OZ PUTS ALL 50 GOVERNORS ON NOTICE OVER BILLIONS LOST TO MEDICAID FRAUD

Their request casts a rather wide net.

The lawmakers want the OIG to scrutinize funding flowing through HHS programs, grants, contracts and sub-awards and determine whether evidence exists of fraud, waste, abuse, misrepresentation or other violations affecting federal health programs.

If misconduct is uncovered, they want the watchdog to consider consequences ranging from administrative remedies and suspension to exclusion from federal healthcare programs or referrals to other authorities.

"Planned Parenthood and its affiliates have faced serious allegations involving the use of federal funds and compliance with federal law. Those allegations deserve a thorough review," Lankford said.

WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD

"The HHS Inspector General should follow the facts, determine whether federal laws and funding requirements have been violated, and hold accountable anyone who has misused taxpayer dollars," he added.

The push comes as the Small Business Administration (SBA) separately reviews more than $88 million in COVID-era Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans received by 38 Planned Parenthood affiliates.

The lawmakers cited the SBA action in their letter, characterizing it as an investigation into whether Planned Parenthood affiliates "illegally received $88 million" in pandemic loans. SBA has described its action as a review of whether the affiliates were eligible for the loans. The review itself is not a finding that the affiliates violated the law.

But the lawmakers want federal scrutiny to go well beyond the pandemic loans.

PLANNED PARENTHOOD OFFERED HORMONES BUT HAD NO ANSWERS WHEN DETRANSITIONER SOUGHT HELP, UNDERCOVER PROBE FINDS

They are asking the OIG to examine Planned Parenthood's broader HHS funding and coordinate with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on what they described as a "comprehensive review" of the organization's activities.

HHS-OIG told Fox News Digital Wednesday evening that it had not yet received the letter.

"We have not received the letter and will review it for appropriate action once received," HHS-OIG said.

Smith, co-chairman of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, said the scrutiny was "long overdue," citing allegations involving federal funding, reporting requirements, sexual exploitation and fetal tissue.

FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP ADMIN OPENS NEW FRONT IN FRAUD CRACKDOWN TARGETING HEALTH INSURERS, DRUG MIDDLEMEN

"It is long overdue for a comprehensive investigation and review, and I urge the HHS OIG to look closely to determine whether it has violated federal standards for federal funding recipients," Smith said.

The congressional letter also points to reports alleging failures to comply with mandatory reporting requirements involving suspected child abuse or neglect. The lawmakers are asking federal officials to examine those allegations. They have not been established as findings by HHS-OIG.

"Given the significant taxpayer resources that flow through federal health and human services programs, it is critical that recipient organizations operate with transparency, integrity, and full compliance with federal standards," the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers closed by asking OIG to coordinate across the federal government to conduct a "comprehensive review" of Planned Parenthood's activities.

"Thank you for your continued commitment to protecting the integrity of federal health programs and safeguarding taxpayer dollars," they wrote.

Planned Parenthood did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Ms Rachel builds sprawling media empire while shelling out thousands to progressive candidates
item.description: Ms. Rachel has donated thousands to progressive political candidates as her popular children's education brand expanded into Netflix, Penguin Random House and Target.
item.content:encoded:
The popular children's YouTuber Rachel Accurso has spent over $22,000 backing Democratic and progressive candidates since 2024, while her toddler-facing brand has expanded into Netflix, Penguin Random House and the toy aisles of Target.

Better known as "Ms. Rachel," the online star has cemented herself as the face of a multimillion-dollar children’s entertainment empire. The former New York City preschool educator, who sings nursery rhymes and teaches language to more than 21 million YouTube subscribers, has also become one of the most politically outspoken figures in her arena, drawing scrutiny for her positions on the Israel-Hamas war, racial issues and various Trump administration immigration policies.

"Ms. Rachel is a children's entertainer, a personality that spawned from the YouTube ecosystem and has now become a fixture alongside other big preschool brands like Sesame Street or Bluey or Cocomelon," James Zahn, editor-in-chief of "The Toy Book," told Fox News Digital.

"For families that have ‘littles,’ as she would say, she's a part of daily life at this point," he added.

MS RACHEL URGES 'EVERY WEALTHY WHITE CELEBRITY' TO MATCH MACKLEMORE'S DONATION TO PALESTINIAN CAUSES

Accurso, 43, launched her YouTube channel in 2019 after finding few media resources for her son, who had a speech delay as a toddler.

Her channel quickly surged in popularity, leading her to create "Songs for Littles," a recurring series in which Accurso — clad in her signature pink shirt, overalls and headband — performs a mix of classic and original children's songs for infants, toddlers and preschoolers.

Her rise to fame has made her one of the most commercially significant figures in American children’s media — and, at the same time, one of the most politically outspoken.

According to federal records, Accurso has donated roughly $22,500 to various Democratic and progressive candidates since 2024, and has made headlines for her outspoken stances on the Israel-Hamas war and other politically charged topics.

MOMS FOR LIBERTY CO-FOUNDER WARNS PARENTS ABOUT MS RACHEL’S POLITICAL ACTIVISM, ‘NOT MR ROGERS’

Accurso has managed to secure deals with Netflix, Penguin Random House Books and Spin Master Toys.

"These companies look at it as: if an entertainer doesn't blur real life into the content, that tends to make things a little bit safer," Zahn said.

Earlier this year, Spin Master debuted a line of toys in collaboration with Accurso — marking yet another feather in her cap as her brand hit the shelves of big-box stores such as Target and Amazon.

"In the years leading up to the announcement of Ms. Rachel's toy deal with Spin Master, there was a bidding war," Zahn said. "So toy and game makers knew that she was a personality with a ton of reach that was worth talking to."

MS RACHEL CONFRONTED ON ACCUSING ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' IN PARK INTERACTION WITH PODCASTER

"I distinctly remember at Toy Fair New York knowing that Ms. Rachel was in the building — not in character, but she was taking meetings," he continued. "And eventually the question became, within the industry: who is going to get the Ms. Rachel toys?"

The line features a variety of toys geared toward both learning and entertainment, with Ms. Rachel personified as a toy-version of herself in several sets.

Her reach has also spread from the online ecosystem into both mainstream and print media after she landed partnerships with Netflix in 2025 and book publisher Penguin Random House in 2024.

"The Ms. Rachel deal with Netflix brings her show to kids who may not otherwise have access to it," Zahn said. "Even though we're in such a screen-heavy world, not every family allows their kids to operate on YouTube."

KAROL MARKOWICZ: MS. RACHEL SAID, 'I AM POLITICAL.' PARENTS SHOULD TAKE HER AT HER WORD

"When we think of media, and we think how digital it is, the analog basis — especially for the younger kids — is very, very key," he added, referring to Accurso’s line of children’s books.

The multi-pronged licensing approach to Accurso’s brand marks a significant — and somewhat unprecedented — shift in children’s entertainment, in which influencers reign in spaces traditionally reserved for mainstream media.

"Today's children, even from the youngest ages, don't just want to watch a television program," David Kleeman, senior vice president of global trends for Dubit, told Fox News Digital. "They want to be part of the media that they consume. They want to play with it. They want to act it out. They want to wear the clothing."

As Accurso’s persona continues to reach into every aspect of a child’s life — from the shows they watch to the toys they play with — Kleeman emphasizes the need for the individual behind the brand to maintain a level of trust with the parents choosing to keep her content in the hands of their children.

MS RACHEL CLAIMS CELEBRITIES SILENT ON GAZA WOULD ‘PROBABLY’ SPEAK IF CHILDREN ‘WERE WHITE’

"Parents have always looked to media as a support for what they’re doing with their kids," Kleeman said. "We tell parents, ‘You’re your child’s first teacher.’ That petrifies a lot of parents, so [they] look for ways to supplement what [they’re] able to do for your child."

However, Accurso’s public politics have made her children’s education brand synonymous with hot-button political issues, such as the ongoing Israel-Hamas war and tensions surrounding Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

She's also put some money behind prominent Democrats.

In 2024, the day after then-President Joe Biden dropped out of the ongoing election and endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris as his Democratic successor, Accurso donated $250 to the Harris Victory Fund.

HOW MS RACHEL'S POLITICAL ACTIVISM IS SPARKING PUSHBACK FROM PARENTS

In the days following, she contributed an additional $750 in funds to Harris for President and the Harris Victory Fund, according to Federal Election Commission records. By September 2024, Accurso had shelled out an additional $2,000 in donations to Harris’ campaign — bringing the total to $3,000 in campaign contributions, records show.

One year later, Accurso made a $5,000 donation to Cameron Kasky’s New York congressional campaign, according to NYC Campaign Finance Board records obtained by Fox News Digital. She was issued a $1,500 refund from Kasky’s campaign on the same day.

Kasky — a survivor of the 2018 high school mass shooting in Parkland, Florida — ran on a platform centered around abolishing ICE, ending military funding to Israel and stricter gun-violence laws.

He ultimately dropped out of the race in January 2026 following a trip to the West Bank, in which he cited a new focus on stopping "settler violence" in the region, according to an X post.

Throughout 2026, campaign finance records show Accurso has spent $12,000 on various New York races with candidates of similar views.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS 'AWESOME' MAMDANI AMID 9/11 MEMORIAL CONTROVERSY, SAYS HE'S VICTIM OF ISLAMOPHOBIC ATTACKS

The children’s educator donated $5,000 to former New York State Assemblymember Yuh-Line Niou’s state Senate campaign, plus an additional $3,500 to Democratic socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier and $4,500 to former New York City Comptroller Brad Lander.

While Niou failed to win in the primaries earlier this year, both Chevalier and Lander won the Democratic nominations for their respective congressional campaigns.

All three candidates have strongly campaigned on platforms that are critical of both Israel and ICE.

Federal Election Commission records also show Accurso gave $3,000 to Abdul El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate campaign in July, marking yet another contribution to a controversial candidate who has repeatedly alleged Israel is committing a "genocide" in Gaza.

DAVID MARCUS: IN BOOMING DETROIT, VOTERS SKEPTICAL OF SOCIALISM SNAKE OIL

"I am political," she said in March, describing her opposition to Immigration and Customs Enforcement. She has been similarly direct about the Israel-Hamas war, drawing scrutiny in 2025 after appearing in a video referring to Palestinian photojournalist Motaz Azaiza as her "friend" — days before Azaiza admitted to withholding footage of Israeli hostages being beaten by a crowd in Gaza on Oct. 7, 2023.

"There isn't a lot of precedent when it comes to a kid's entertainer making comments outside of their content that rub people the wrong way — or in some cases the right way," Zahn said.

The YouTuber’s checkbook tells a similar story, with her net worth reportedly estimated at around $50 million. Last year, Forbes’ 2025 Top Creators List ranked Accurso at No. 20 with a whopping $23 million in annual earnings.

The dollar figures — and subsequent brand deals — signify an apparent fan separation between Ms. Rachel as a brand and Accurso as a public figure.

"It's always an issue when you have a presenter who is basically presenting as themselves," Kleeman told Fox News Digital. "Mr. Rogers just was ‘Mr. Rogers.’ There was no character or artifice there. Ms. Rachel has created ‘Ms. Rachel,’ as opposed to Rachel Accurso."

"Viewers often have a problem separating that real-life person from the character," he added.

MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH

The sentiment was echoed by Zahn, who suggests that Accurso’s high-profile political stances are doing little to deter brands from signing her YouTube persona.

"Companies can take multiple approaches, as we've seen with other celebrity controversies," Zahn said. "They can choose to back the celebrity, they can push back from the celebrity, they can distance themselves from it, or they can say nothing at all. And sometimes saying nothing at all is what it really needs."

While parents may be keyed into Accurso’s views on topics such as Gaza and gender representation, Kleeman argues that as long as the content creator keeps politics out of her educational materials, she will likely feel little pushback from both brands and fans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"I think she's been very careful to keep what she puts out to children focused on the child development, on the learning, on the play," Kleeman told Fox News Digital. "I think that Netflix or any channel that’s carrying content that’s being presented by a real person is going to have to balance how well that person is conveying what it is they’re transmitting to kids — the specific children’s content, not the things that go around it."

Fox News Digital reached out to Accurso, Netflix, Penguin Random House and Spin Master for comment.

item.title: JONATHAN TURLEY: Justice Alito blazes the ethical path the Supreme Court should take
item.description: Key recusal from the Suncor Energy climate change case leaves only eight justices, raising the stakes for a potential 4-4 split that could open floodgates for lawsuits.
item.content:encoded:
On Sept. 28, Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito recused himself from one of the term's most important cases: Suncor Energy Inc. v. County Commissioners of Boulder County. As I have previously discussed, the case involving the liability of energy companies for nuisance actions tied to climate change could have sweeping implications for the country. Justice Alito should be commended for avoiding even the appearance of a personal interest or a conflict in the case. However, the controversy should prompt the court to explore a longstanding problem for justices holding financial interests that can conflict with their duties. The solution is simple: Justices need to use blind trusts.

Supreme Court Clerk Scott Harris released a letter revealing that Alito decided he "will not continue to participate" in Suncor Energy Inc. v. County Commissioners of Boulder County.

Boulder, sued energy companies under "theories of public and private nuisance, trespass, unjust enrichment, and civil conspiracy, claiming that they knowingly contributed to climate change while misleading the public about its impacts." The Colorado Supreme Court ruled for the city and the county in finding that such lawsuits are not barred by federal preemption. If such lawsuits are allowed to go forward, it would expose companies to potentially thousands of climate change lawsuits. Oral argument is set for Oct. 5.

SUPREME COURT CAN RESTORE SANITY AND STOP THE LEFT’S RADICAL CLIMATE AGENDA

The recusal is a blow for challengers who believe that the opinion could be close, and Alito was believed to be on the side of barring such actions. It is now down to eight justices, so a single loss of another conservative could result in a 4-4 tie – leaving the lower court decision unchanged.

While the letter did not give a reason, critics had called for Alito's recusal due to his financial interest in energy companies which could benefit from the decision.

CONSERVATIVE GROUPS SAY JUSTICE KAGAN CANNOT BE IMPARTIAL IN UPCOMING SUPREME COURT CLIMATE LITIGATION

That included 30 organizations which jointly asked the Senate Judiciary Committee to investigate his involvement in the case. Notably, the court responded to media inquiries by declaring that Alito had no financial interest in any party to the case and that legal counsel had told him that there is no need to recuse himself.

Yet, the standard is whether a reasonable person could question his impartiality and, while he had no interest in the parties, he appears to have investments in other energy companies. Alito previously withdrew shortly before arguments in a separate oil industry case earlier this year.

JUSTICE NEIL GORSUCH BREAKS SILENCE ON VIOLENT THREATS AGAINST JUDICIARY, SUPREME COURT LEAKS

The Ethics in Government Act of 1978 (EIGA) established financial disclosure reporting requirements for many high-level government officials and employees, including the Justices of the Supreme Court. Supreme Court Justices file publicly available financial disclosure statements that report certain financial transactions. However, they are not required to put their investments into blind trusts.

Justices should be able to have investment portfolios, but they can hold such investments in blind trusts or qualified blind trusts. In a blind trust, the justice will "have no control over, will receive no communications about, and will (eventually as existing assets are sold and new ones obtained by the trustee) have no knowledge of the identity of the specific assets held in the trust. As such, once a blind trust is established and new assets obtained, an official will not need to (and will not be able to) identify the particular assets 13 5 C.F.R. § 2635.403(b)."

LIBERAL JUSTICE HAMMERS SUPREME COURT FOR FAST-TRACKING EMERGENCY DOCKET CASES

Other federal officials must use such trusts and there is no reason why justices should be exempt, in my view. This has been a continual and embarrassing problem. Years ago, the court affirmed an appellate ruling in a major case involving a $400 billion lawsuit in American Isuzu Motors v. Ntsebeza (2008) without a hearing after four justices had to recuse themselves (Chief Justice John Roberts Jr. and Justices Anthony Kennedy, Stephen Breyer, and Samuel Alito Jr).

The business interests of justices should not interfere with the business of the court. You should either be an active investor in the markets or a justice, not both. The public has a reasonable expectation that, in seeking this high office, justices are willing to set aside certain privileges or interests. This is one of them.

This is not to cast aspersions on the justices. These recusals show that members, including Alito, are cognizant and committed to avoiding even the appearance of a conflict of interest. Moreover, some judges and justices resolve this question by using diversified mutual funds or ETFs, where the justice does not control the micro-allocations within the fund. However, there is still knowledge of financial interests in given areas.

This is not a costless obligation for justices. Blind trusts add costs (which Congress may want to consider defraying) and can be complex. However, the business of the court is too important to be routinely compromised or complicated by these financial interests.

While legislation has been introduced along these lines, it would be simpler for justices to voluntarily adopt this practice.

Consider it is the price of being one of nine. If you want to sit on this court, you have to do justice, which is only fully possible if your investments, like justice itself, are blind.
